claude.sample_unit: residents (53 preworkshop, 44 postworkshop survey respondents; 72 eligible)

links.outcome: Resident confidence appraising AI output and concern about inaccuracy and bias
links.effect: Unpaired, descriptive only. Confidence appraising AI output 79.5% vs. 60.4%; concern about inaccurate predictions 88.6% vs. 69.8%; concern about population-level bias 88.6% vs. 77.4%; 90.5% rated session 4 or 5.
links.quote: Postworkshop respondents more often agreed or strongly agreed that they were confident in critically appraising AI output (79.5% vs. 60.4%), concerned about inaccurate predictions (88.6% vs. 69.8%), and concerned about population-level bias (88.6% vs. 77.4%).

openai.sample_unit: anonymous, unpaired survey responses (53 preworkshop and 44 postworkshop)

links.outcome: Self-reported confidence in critically appraising AI output
links.effect: Confidence was 60.4% preworkshop and 79.5% postworkshop. Results were descriptive and unpaired; objective appraisal skills, clinical behavior, and patient outcomes were not assessed.
links.quote: Confidence critically appraising AI output increased from 60.4% preworkshop to 79.5% postworkshop.

links.outcome: Resident concern about inaccurate AI predictions and population-level bias
links.effect: Concern about inaccurate predictions increased from 69.8% to 88.6%, and concern about population-level bias from 77.4% to 88.6%; these were descriptive comparisons of unpaired self-reports.
links.quote: Postworkshop respondents more often agreed or strongly agreed that they were confident in critically appraising AI output (79.5% vs. 60.4%), concerned about inaccurate predictions (88.6% vs. 69.8%), and concerned about population-level bias (88.6% vs. 77.4%).
